import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_76/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_76/training_1.csv"

df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source5_76_0 and Source5_76_1 on "school_name"
joined_df = pd.merge(df0, df1, on="school_name", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by Source5_76_1.school_name and aggregation avg(Source5_76_1.reading_score)
# Since after join, school_name column is from both tables but identical, we use joined_df.school_name
result = joined_df.groupby("school_name", as_index=False)["reading_score"].mean()

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
result = result.rename(columns={"reading_score": "reading_score", "school_name": "school_name"})

# Ensure data types match target schema: school_name as string, reading_score as float
result["school_name"] = result["school_name"].astype(str)
result["reading_score"] = result["reading_score"].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_76/target_multisource.csv"
result.to_csv(target_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source files with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_76/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length5_76/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source5_76_0 and Source5_76_1 on school_name (inner join)
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, how='inner', left_on='school_name', right_on='school_name')

# Group by school_name and aggregate average reading_score
result = joined.groupby('school_name', as_index=False).agg({'reading_score': 'mean'})

# Ensure column order and names exactly as target schema
result = result[['school_name', 'reading_score']]
